decisions.rationale: Leading Swampert and Tsareena with Pelipper and Archaludon in back. Tsareena's Queenly Majesty blocks priority (Fake Out, Quash) and her Grass typing grants immunity to Sleep Powder. Swampert can Protect Turn 1 against potential Sun attacks. Holding Pelipper in back allows us to manually switch Pelipper in after Charizard Mega Evolves to permanently overwrite Sun with Rain, enabling Swift Swim for Swampert and 1-turn Electro Shot for Archaludon.
decisions.notebook: Charizard-Mega-Y: Timid, Charizardite Y (Heat Wave, Solar Beam, Air Slash, Protect). Venusaur: Modest, Focus Sash, Chlorophyll (Energy Ball, Sludge Bomb, Sleep Powder, Protect). Raichu: Timid, Sitrus Berry, Lightning Rod (Fake Out, Electroweb, Encore, Protect). Tauros-Paldea-Aqua: Jolly, Wacan Berry, Intimidate (Close Combat, Liquidation, Aqua Jet, Protect). Kingambit: Black Glasses, Defiant (Kowtow Cleave, Iron Head, Low Kick, Protect). Sableye: Mental Herb, Prankster (Taunt, Will-O-Wisp, Quash, Recover). Plan G3: Lead Swampert + Tsareena to block Fake Out/Prankster and Sleep Powder. Keep Pelipper in back to manually switch in AFTER Charizard Megas, replacing Sun with Rain to enable Swampert Swift Swim and Archaludon Electro Shot.

decisions.rationale: Lead Mega Charizard Y plus Venusaur pressures the expected Pelipper/Swampert rain lead immediately by replacing rain with sun and threatening both slots. Raichu provides speed control, Encore, and Lightning Rod support; Kingambit gives strong endgame pressure into Archaludon and Galarian Slowking.

Swampert Protects while Mega Evolving to preserve HP against Charizard Y's Solar Beam and Venusaur's Grass/Poison attacks. Tsareena switches to Archaludon, which safely resists Venusaur's STABs (immune to Sludge Bomb, 0.25x to Energy Ball) and Charizard's Flying/Grass coverage. On Turn 2, Pelipper can switch in after Charizard has already Mega Evolved, overwriting Sun with Rain to enable Archaludon's Electro Shot and Swampert's Swift Swim.
decisions.notebook: G3: Turn 1 Swampert Mega Protect + Tsareena -> Archaludon switch. Turn 2 plan: switch Swampert to Pelipper to overwrite Sun with Rain after Charizard Y's Drought has already resolved.

decisions.rationale: Mega Charizard Y establishes sun before attacks. Chlorophyll Venusaur’s Energy Ball is a guaranteed OHKO on Mega Swampert, while sun-boosted Heat Wave heavily pressures Tsareena and is much stronger than Sludge Bomb if Swampert protects.
decisions.notebook: Pelipper is Focus Sash Drizzle with Tailwind; respect it as the rain/speed-control enabler. Archaludon revealed Stamina and Wise Glasses. Tsareena's Queenly Majesty blocks priority. Mega Swampert is slower than Mega Charizard Y and sun-boosted Chlorophyll Venusaur, and both Charizard Y Solar Beam and Venusaur Energy Ball threaten an OHKO. Against this rain mode, favor the Charizard Y/Venusaur sun core and maintain sun access. Garganacl has Wide Guard and Purifying Salt; avoid relying on spread attacks or Sleep Powder into it. In sun, Venusaur Energy Ball guarantees the Mega Swampert OHKO; Mega Charizard Y Heat Wave does 93.9–172.8% to Tsareena as a spread hit, while Venusaur Sludge Bomb does 64.8–118.4%.

decisions.rationale: Swampert is threatened by 4x Grass moves under Sun from both Charizard-Y and Venusaur, and Swampert's Protect is at reduced accuracy. Switching Swampert to Pelipper sets Rain via Drizzle, neutralizing Venusaur's Chlorophyll speed boost and weakening Fire moves. Archaludon uses Protect at 12% HP to safely survive Turn 2 attacks.
decisions.notebook: G3 T1: Swampert Mega Protect, Tsareena -> Archaludon. G3 T2: Swampert -> Pelipper (Drizzle sets Rain), Archaludon Protects. Rain active for T3. Swampert in back ready with Swift Swim.

decisions.rationale: Venusaur’s sun-boosted Energy Ball is a guaranteed OHKO on Mega Swampert before it can move. Charizard’s Air Slash is a guaranteed KO on the 11% Archaludon and is more accurate than Heat Wave, securing both knockouts unless Swampert succeeds on consecutive Protect.
decisions.notebook: Against the Swampert/Archaludon lead under Charizard Y sun, Chlorophyll Venusaur outspeeds both. Venusaur Energy Ball guarantees an OHKO on Mega Swampert in sun; Charizard Y Air Slash guarantees a KO on Archaludon from 11% and has 95% accuracy. Pelipper is Focus Sash Drizzle with Tailwind; preserve Charizard Y’s sun pressure against rain mode. Garganacl has Wide Guard and Purifying Salt, so avoid depending on spread attacks or Sleep Powder into it. Tsareena has Queenly Majesty, which blocks priority. Archaludon is Stamina with Wise Glasses.

decisions.rationale: Pelipper uses Protect to preserve its remaining HP and block incoming attacks targeting slot 1. Charizard outspeeds Archaludon (119 vs 132-167) and KOs its 12% HP, while consecutive Protect on Archaludon is unreliable (~33%). Switching Archaludon to Tsareena absorbs Venusaur's Grass attacks safely due to its Grass resistance, protecting Swampert-Mega from taking heavy 4x Grass damage on a switch and preserving Swampert at 100% HP to sweep in Rain next turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Pelipper setting Rain empowers Mega Swampert (Swift Swim 208 Speed outspeeds Charizard-Y 132-167 and Venusaur 100-132). Swampert Rain Waterfall 100% OHKOs Charizard-Y. Opponent leads Charizard-Mega-Y + Venusaur (Sash). Tsareena safely switches into Grass moves to preserve Swampert.

decisions.rationale: Switching in Swampert-Mega gives us full board control in Rain. With Swift Swim active (208 Speed), Swampert outspeeds both Charizard-Mega-Y (132-167) and Venusaur (100-132). Rain-boosted Waterfall guarantees an OHKO on Charizard-Mega-Y, while Solar Beam from Charizard requires a two-turn charge outside Sun.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Pelipper set Rain (4 turns left). Mega Swampert (Swift Swim 208 Speed) outspeeds Charizard-Y and Venusaur in Rain. Rain Waterfall 100% OHKOs Charizard-Y. Charizard-Y cannot single-turn Solar Beam in Rain.

decisions.rationale: Air Slash guarantees Archaludon’s KO from 11%, and Energy Ball guarantees Pelipper’s KO from 23%. Charizard moves before Venusaur; splitting attacks covers either foe using Protect, while Archaludon’s repeated Protect has reduced success.
decisions.notebook: Against the Swampert/Archaludon lead under Charizard Y sun, Chlorophyll Venusaur outspeeds both. Venusaur Energy Ball guarantees an OHKO on Mega Swampert in sun; Charizard Y Air Slash guarantees a KO on Archaludon from 11% and has 95% accuracy. Pelipper is Focus Sash Drizzle with Tailwind; preserve Charizard Y’s sun pressure against rain mode. Garganacl has Wide Guard and Purifying Salt, so avoid depending on spread attacks or Sleep Powder into it. Tsareena has Queenly Majesty, which blocks priority. Archaludon is Stamina with Wise Glasses. Venusaur Energy Ball guarantees Pelipper’s KO from 23% even in rain.

decisions.rationale: In Rain, Swampert-Mega (208 Speed) outspeeds both Charizard-Y and Venusaur. Rain-boosted Waterfall guarantees an OHKO on Charizard-Y before it can act, permanently eliminating the opponent's weather setter. Pelipper uses 100%-accurate Hurricane into Venusaur to chunk it or break its Focus Sash.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Rain active (3 turns left). Mega Swampert (Swift Swim, 208 Speed) outspeeds Timid Charizard-Y and Modest Venusaur. Waterfall OHKOs Charizard-Y in Rain. Rain Hurricane has 100% accuracy into Venusaur.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Cover both immediate threats: Air Slash removes Pelipper unless its reduced-success Protect lands, while Energy Ball targets Mega Swampert for the crucial 4x KO. Either opposing Protect still leaves the other foe removed, preserving a decisive advantage.
decisions.notebook: Mega Swampert is the rain-mode centerpiece: Swift Swim makes it faster than the current team in rain, while Venusaur’s Energy Ball is the primary 4x answer. Pelipper carries Focus Sash, Drizzle, Tailwind, Hurricane, Hydro Pump, and Protect; it can be finished from low HP by Venusaur Energy Ball. Charizard Y’s Air Slash cleanly finishes weak Archaludon; preserve Charizard’s Drought pressure when possible. Archaludon is Stamina with Wise Glasses. Tsareena’s Queenly Majesty blocks priority. Garganacl has Wide Guard and Purifying Salt, so avoid relying on spread damage or Sleep Powder into it. Raichu offers Lightning Rod, Fake Out, Electroweb, Encore, and speed; Kingambit supplies Dark/Steel pressure and Defiant.

decisions.rationale: Kingambit is the robust endgame piece: it can reliably remove the weakened Pelipper and is far better equipped than Raichu to finish Archaludon alone, resisting its Steel-, Dragon-, and Electric-type attacks.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 revealed Pelipper’s Focus Sash has been consumed; it has Hurricane, Hydro Pump, Tailwind, and Protect. Mega Swampert is the rain-mode centerpiece with Swift Swim, but Venusaur’s Energy Ball cleanly answers it. Archaludon is Stamina with Wise Glasses and has Electro Shot, Draco Meteor, Flash Cannon, Protect; it was heavily chipped by Charizard Y Heat Wave. Tsareena has Queenly Majesty, blocking priority. Charizard Y’s Drought can overwrite rain when it Mega Evolves, but it is vulnerable to rain-boosted Waterfall. Raichu provides Lightning Rod, Fake Out, Electroweb, Encore, and Protect, but has limited direct damage into Archaludon; preserve Kingambit for Steel/Dragon endgames when possible. Garganacl has Wide Guard and Purifying Salt, so do not rely on spread damage or Sleep Powder into it.

decisions.rationale: Both Archaludon (119 Speed) and Pelipper (115 Speed) outspeed Kingambit (70-102 Speed). In Rain, Electro Shot executes immediately, dealing 37.2-67.4% and granting Archaludon +1 SpA. Pelipper's Rain Hydro Pump deals 52.7-97.7% to Kingambit. Combining both attacks into Kingambit overwhelms it before it can move, and even if Hydro Pump misses or Pelipper faints to Venusaur, Archaludon's +1 SpA Electro Shot guarantees the finish on Turn 6.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Rain active (2 turns left). Pelipper 115 Speed, Archaludon 119 Speed both outspeed Kingambit (70-102 Speed). Rain Electro Shot executes in 1 turn and gives +1 SpA. Rain Hydro Pump deals 52.7-97.7% into Kingambit.

decisions.rationale: Protect Venusaur from the immediate double-target while Kingambit’s Low Kick guarantees Archaludon’s KO if it does not Protect. This also avoids a confusion self-hit from Venusaur at 1 HP; Raichu remains a strong cleanup option versus Pelipper.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Pelipper’s Focus Sash is consumed; it has Hurricane, Hydro Pump, Tailwind, Protect, and Drizzle. Mega Swampert is the rain centerpiece with Swift Swim, but Venusaur Energy Ball cleanly answers it. Archaludon is Stamina with Wise Glasses and has Electro Shot, Draco Meteor, Flash Cannon, Protect; Kingambit Low Kick is an effective endgame answer. Tsareena has Queenly Majesty, blocking priority. Raichu provides Lightning Rod, Fake Out, Electroweb, Encore, and Protect; preserve Kingambit for Steel/Dragon endgames. Garganacl has Wide Guard and Purifying Salt, so avoid relying on spread damage or Sleep Powder into it.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Both Pelipper (24% HP) and Archaludon (12% HP) are in low HP ranges vulnerable to Raichu's incoming Fake Out and spread/coverage damage. Both of our Pokémon have fresh Protects available after not protecting on turn 5. Double Protecting safely wastes Raichu's Fake Out turn, protects against Electroweb/Energy Ball, and lets Venusaur potentially take confusion self-damage at 1% HP.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Opponent has Raichu (100% HP, Sitrus Berry, LightningRod) and Venusaur (1% HP, confused) remaining. Kingambit and Charizard-Y fainted. Raichu entered Turn 5.

decisions.rationale: Electroweb guarantees Pelipper’s KO from 23% while lowering Archaludon’s Speed. Energy Ball is Venusaur’s only damaging option into Archaludon and can finish it after Electroweb; even if Venusaur fails confusion or is KOed, the Speed drop leaves Raichu positioned to clean the weakened Archaludon.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 revealed: Pelipper is Focus Sash (consumed), Drizzle, with Hurricane/Hydro Pump/Tailwind/Protect. Mega Swampert is Swift Swim with Waterfall/High Horsepower/Ice Punch/Protect. Archaludon is Stamina, Wise Glasses, with Electro Shot/Draco Meteor/Flash Cannon/Protect. Tsareena has Queenly Majesty, blocking priority. Opponent’s unbrought Slowking-Galar is Regenerator Sitrus with Sludge Bomb/Chilly Reception/Psychic Noise/Protect; Garganacl is Purifying Salt Leftovers with Salt Cure/Rock Slide/Wide Guard/Recover. Preserve awareness that Garganacl can Wide Guard and is immune to status from Purifying Salt.

decisions.rationale: Raichu is the main threat that outspeeds Archaludon and threatens to sweep with Electroweb if left alive. Archaludon's +1 Wise Glasses Draco Meteor guarantees an OHKO on Raichu (106.6-205.2%) and bypasses LightningRod. Flash Cannon into Venusaur would leave Raichu alive to outspeed and KO Archaludon on Turn 8. Pelipper uses 80% accuracy Hydro Pump into 1% HP Venusaur to remove it if Raichu Protects or Encores instead of attacking Pelipper.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Raichu is Timid with Sitrus Berry, LightningRod, and moves FakeOut/Electroweb/Encore/Protect. Venusaur is Modest with 1% HP remaining.

decisions.rationale: Electroweb guarantees Pelipper’s KO if it does not Protect and leaves Archaludon in range of Energy Ball; if Archaludon moves first, Raichu still gets the decisive spread chip before Venusaur falls. Repeated Protects are reduced, and this line covers either target attempting one.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 sets confirmed: Pelipper is Focus Sash Drizzle with Hurricane/Hydro Pump/Tailwind/Protect; Mega Swampert is Swift Swim with Waterfall/High Horsepower/Ice Punch/Protect; Archaludon is Stamina Wise Glasses with Electro Shot/Draco Meteor/Flash Cannon/Protect; Tsareena has Queenly Majesty. Slowking-Galar is Regenerator Sitrus with Sludge Bomb/Chilly Reception/Psychic Noise/Protect; Garganacl is Purifying Salt Leftovers with Salt Cure/Rock Slide/Wide Guard/Recover. Archaludon’s boosted Wise Glasses Draco Meteor can OHKO Raichu; Lightning Rod absorbs its Electro Shot. Raichu Electroweb always KOs Pelipper from roughly one-quarter health and substantially chips Archaludon; pair it with Venusaur Energy Ball when possible. Respect reduced but still possible repeated Protects.

decisions.rationale: Raichu outspeeds Pelipper (143-178 vs 115) and Electroweb KOs Pelipper at 24% HP. Raichu entered turn 5, so Fake Out is invalid. Protect only delays the inevitable turn without changing board conditions. Pelipper's highest win percentage comes from Hydro Pump into Raichu, banking on Electroweb missing (95% accuracy) and Hydro Pump landing (or critting).
decisions.notebook: Game 3 concluded.

decisions.rationale: Encore Pelipper’s last-used Hydro Pump to remove its access to Protect and force inaccurate attacks; this preserves the clearest path for Raichu to finish it with Electroweb.
decisions.notebook: Pelipper’s Focus Sash was not triggered by Venusaur’s Energy Ball, so it may still survive a would-be KO at full effect. In a Raichu endgame, Encore its last move before attempting repeated Electroweb pressure when possible; locking Hydro Pump denies Protect but forces its 80%-accurate attack.

decisions.rationale: Raichu is the opponent's last Pokémon. Pelipper is locked into Hydro Pump by Encore. Targeting Raichu (foe 1) with Hydro Pump is our only remaining line to win if Raichu misses or uses a non-damaging move.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 conclusion: Opponent brought Charizard-Mega-Y, Venusaur, Kingambit, and Raichu. Raichu carried Fake Out, Electroweb, Encore, Protect with Sitrus Berry and LightningRod.

decisions.rationale: Electroweb acts before Pelipper and is 4x super-effective; it cleanly removes the lone remaining foe before its Encored Hydro Pump can move.
decisions.notebook: Pelipper is Modest Drizzle with Focus Sash not yet confirmed consumed; its revealed moves are Hurricane, Hydro Pump, Tailwind, Protect. Encore can lock it into Hydro Pump, denying Protect but forcing an 80%-accurate attack. Raichu is Timid with Fake Out, Electroweb, Encore, and Protect; preserve it for Pelipper endgames.

reflections.summary: The game and series were lost because relying on Mega Swampert into a Sun/Chlorophyll core paired with Raichu backfired. Trading Mega Swampert early to remove Mega Charizard Y left the team exposed to Chlorophyll Venusaur and Raichu's LightningRod/Encore control once rain expired. Prep over-indexed on standard rain offense, failing to account for how effectively Raichu and Venusaur neutralize Archaludon and Pelipper in the endgame.
reflections.adjustment: Pivot away from Mega Swampert and heavy rain offense against this Sun/LightningRod composition. Bring Mimikyu from the draft roster for Trick Room to reverse Chlorophyll Speed boosts, or leverage Garganacl to stall out sun turns. If using Pelipper, conserve weather active turns and bring Scrafty or Tsareena in positions where they can directly remove Raichu and Kingambit without relying on special electric or water moves.
reflections.notebook: Opponent core: Mega Charizard Y, Focus Sash Chlorophyll Venusaur (Energy Ball, Sludge Bomb, Sleep Powder), LightningRod Sitrus Raichu (Fake Out, Electroweb, Encore, Protect), and BlackGlasses Kingambit. Raichu nullifies Archaludon via LightningRod and locks passive attackers with Encore and Electroweb. Sun-boosted Chlorophyll Venusaur outspeeds and OHKOs Mega Swampert. Rematch prep: Leave Mega Swampert on the bench against Venusaur/Sun cores; register Mimikyu for Trick Room speed control and Scrafty for immediate physical fighting pressure against Kingambit and Raichu.

reflections.summary: Won the game and series 2-1 because Venusaur traded favorably into Mega Swampert despite losing Charizard, then Raichu’s Electroweb speed control and Encore prevented Pelipper from safely Protecting and secured the endgame. The Charizard-Y/Venusaur/Raichu core was fundamentally effective, though Mega Charizard Y was exposed to Swampert’s Waterfall and did not last long. Kingambit contributed little in the revealed sequence. No evidence of specific between-game adjustments was supplied, so their effect cannot be isolated; the decisive factors were the selected anti-rain tools and clean execution.
reflections.adjustment: For a rematch, retain Venusaur and Raichu as priority answers to Swampert/Pelipper: Venusaur’s Focus Sash plus Grass coverage can remove Swampert, while Raichu should be preserved for Pelipper control and endgames. Reconsider leading or Mega Evolving Charizard Y directly into Mega Swampert unless it has strong protection or positioning; Drought support is valuable, but Charizard is vulnerable to Waterfall. Evaluate Paldean Tauros-Aqua or Sableye during preview as alternatives if they provide a safer rain matchup or disruption. The registered six generally contained the right tools, especially Venusaur and Raichu; there is insufficient evidence that Dragonite, Altaria, Emolga, or Avalugg would have improved this matchup.
reflections.notebook: Opponent’s rain core is Mega Swampert, Focus Sash Modest Pelipper, and Modest Wise Glasses Archaludon. Pelipper revealed Hurricane, Hydro Pump, Tailwind, and Protect; Encore can deny its Protect and force Hydro Pump. Archaludon revealed Electro Shot, Draco Meteor, Flash Cannon, Protect, and Stamina; it can use Protect to buy Electro Shot pressure, but low-HP Archaludon can still be finished by Venusaur’s Energy Ball. Tsareena carries Queenly Majesty and Helping Hand alongside Power Whip, High Jump Kick, and Knock Off, so do not rely on priority into it. Venusaur with Focus Sash and Energy Ball is a strong Mega Swampert answer; Raichu’s Electroweb and Encore are especially valuable to preserve for Pelipper endgames. Charizard Y’s sun is useful disruption, but it must avoid direct exposure to Swampert Waterfall.
